W.note: 5-7-5 (Win-ter dusk sun gone; moth-er-of-pearl on thin cloud; the lake ice holds it), nacreous glow at winter dusk caught in lake ice is a quiet, earned turn though 'thin cloud' is a bit vague.

X.note: Line 1 is 6 syllables (pearl-lit moth-er-of-pearl) so 6-7-5, redundant 'pearl' phrasing, and 'ice dreams in the dark' is stock-poetic.

Y.note: 5-7-5 (Lens cloud on the ridge; the whole gale runs through its shape; ice cracks underfoot), accurate lenticular standing-wave insight but the final line's cut feels abrupt and loosely connected.

Z.note: 5-7-5 (Moth-er-of-pearl sky; na-cre-ous clouds hold the sun; long af-ter it sets), accurate and clean but fairly plain with 'mother-of-pearl' a stock phrase.
